assumptions: Customer-consented telemetry exports or APIs can be obtained for an initial cross-brand sample.
At least one institutional payer experiences losses large enough to justify recurring monitoring.
The founder can limit manual review sufficiently to preserve software-like margins.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A permissioned 20-system pilot showing reproducible fault detection, quantified recovered value, low false-positive rates, and at least two paid renewals or institutional monitoring commitments.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Independent cross-brand evidence can resolve the trust gap between vendor telemetry, modeled output, and remediation responsibility.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Lost yield and warranty disputes create measurable value, but the frequency, recoverable loss, and best-paying institutional customer remain unvalidated.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid checks and recurring monitoring could support strong margins, yet connector, analyst, liability, and acquisition costs are assumptions and the 25,000-asset path is demanding.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: A consented installer pilot is narrow and reachable, but the initial residential segment may have low willingness to pay and the institutional beachhead is not selected.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Vendor-neutral verification is differentiated, though vendors, installers, and existing monitoring providers can cover much of the workflow.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Validated performance data can extend from commissioning into portfolio diligence, warranty support, insurance, lending, and commercial assets.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Permissioned fault signatures and remediation outcomes could compound, but telemetry access is nonexclusive, revocable, and vendor-dependent.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Independence and cross-brand diagnosis may improve trust and remediation, but superiority over portal analytics has not been quantified.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Growing paired PV-storage deployment increases the installed base and complexity that require performance verification.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Family-installer access enables a credible pilot, while scalable access to distributors, lenders, or insurers is still hypothetical.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder fits time-series analytics and can outsource fieldwork, but lawful telemetry, normalization, API stability, and attribution liability are material risks.

highest_value_structural_change: Choose one institutional beachhead and secure durable portfolio telemetry rights plus outcome-linked remediation data under a multi-year contract.
main_structural_strength: The service ties independent, cross-brand analytics to measurable asset underperformance and recurring remediation evidence.
primary_score_limiter: The business lacks durable telemetry control and validated willingness to pay from a clearly selected institutional customer.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Vendor portals already expose production data, while weather and household-load variance can make incremental diagnosis and savings attribution contentious.
